examples.ko: 할아버지의 걸음은 느릿느릿해요.
examples.en: Grandpa's walk is slow and unhurried.

examples.ko: 더운 날에는 몸도 마음도 느릿느릿해져요.
examples.en: On hot days both body and mind become sluggish.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말투가 느릿느릿해서 답답할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: His way of speaking is slow, so it can be frustrating at times.

examples.ko: 동작이 느릿느릿한 고양이가 창가에 누워 있어요.
examples.en: A cat with lazy movements is lying by the window.

examples.ko: 오늘따라 컴퓨터가 느릿느릿해요.
examples.en: The computer is sluggish today.

examples.ko: 느릿느릿하던 동생이 갑자기 달리기 시작했어요.
examples.en: My slow-moving sibling suddenly started running.

explain: 행동이나 말이 아주 느리고 굼뜬 모습이에요. 실제로는 부사 '느릿느릿'을 훨씬 많이 써서 '느릿느릿 걷다'처럼 말해요. 형용사는 상태를 설명할 때 써요.

phrases.en: Grandmother walks very slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사 '느릿느릿'이 훨씬 자주 쓰여서 동사 앞에 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb 느릿느릿 is used much more often, placed before a verb.

phrases.en: I went home with slow steps.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때는 '-ㄴ' 활용형을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the -ㄴ form to describe a noun that follows.

phrases.en: On hot days my body becomes sluggish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점점 느려지는 상태의 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone or something gradually becomes slow.

explain_en: It describes behavior or speech that is very slow and dragging. In reality the adverb '느릿느릿' is used far more often, as in '느릿느릿 걷다'. The adjective form is for describing a state.

examples.ko: 새 옷을 몸에 대보고 사세요.
examples.en: Hold the new clothes up against your body before you buy them.

examples.ko: 두 사진을 나란히 대보면 차이가 보여요.
examples.en: If you hold the two photos side by side, you can see the difference.

examples.ko: 이 자를 책상에 대봐서 길이를 재 봤어요.
examples.en: I put this ruler against the desk to measure the length.

examples.ko: 구두를 발에 대봤는데 너무 작았어요.
examples.en: I held the shoes up to my foot, and they were too small.

examples.ko: 친구 키와 제 키를 대봤더니 제가 더 컸어요.
examples.en: When I measured my height against my friend's, I was taller.

examples.ko: 액자를 벽에 대본 다음에 못을 박았어요.
examples.en: I held the frame against the wall and then drove in the nail.

explain: 두 물건을 나란히 맞대 보거나 몸에 대 보면서 크기, 색, 길이를 확인할 때 써요. 말이나 머릿속으로 견줄 때는 '비교하다'를 써요. '대보다'는 실제로 손으로 갖다 대는 동작이 있을 때 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I held the clothes up against my body and then bought them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 살 때 먼저 몸에 맞는지 확인하는 동작과 같이 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly said when checking whether clothes fit before buying them.
phrases.en_equiv: to try it against yourself and then buy

phrases.en: When I put a ruler against them, the lengths are different.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-니까'를 붙이면 대 본 뒤에 알게 된 사실을 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-니까' lets you state what you found out after comparing.
phrases.en_equiv: to hold a ruler against it

phrases.en: Hold this skirt up against your body.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구에게 같이 해 보자고 권할 때 쓰는 말투예요. 더 높이면 '대보세요'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A friendly way to suggest trying something; the polite form is '대보세요'.

explain_en: It is used when you physically hold one thing against another or against your body to check size, color, or length. For comparing in words or in your head, use '비교하다'. '대보다' fits when there is an actual action of holding something up.

t90.ax: I put this ruler against the desk to measure the length.

en: to not know; to be ignorant; to have no idea

examples.ko: 멋모르고 시작했다가 일이 너무 커졌어요.
examples.en: I started without knowing what I was getting into, and it got too big.

examples.ko: 멋모르는 신입이라 실수가 많았어요.
examples.en: I was a clueless newcomer, so I made many mistakes.

examples.ko: 처음 가는 곳이라 멋모르면 길을 잃기 쉬워요.
examples.en: It's a place you've never been, so it's easy to get lost if you don't know the area.

examples.ko: 멋모르던 때는 모든 게 쉬워 보였어요.
examples.en: When I didn't know any better, everything looked easy.

examples.ko: 멋모르고 산 물건이라 어떻게 쓰는지 몰라요.
examples.en: I bought it without knowing what it was, so I don't know how to use it.

examples.ko: 멋모르는 외국인이라고 바가지를 씌우면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't overcharge someone just because they're a clueless foreigner.

explain: 일이 어떻게 돌아가는지, 속사정을 모르는 채로 하는 상황에 써요. 거의 '멋모르고', '멋모르는 + 명사' 꼴로 쓰고, '모르다'처럼 '르' 불규칙이라 해요체는 '멋몰라요'예요. '모르고'보다 상황을 몰라서 순진하거나 무심하게 한다는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: I followed my friend without knowing anything and had a hard time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '멋모르고' 뒤에 행동을 붙여서 사정을 모른 채 한 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put an action after '멋모르고' to describe something done without knowing the situation.

phrases.en: A child who didn't know any better joined the adults' conversation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '멋모르는' 뒤에 사람을 붙여서 사정을 모르는 순진한 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '멋모르는' before a person describes someone naive who does not know how things work.

phrases.en: If you rush in without knowing what you're doing, you could get hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘 모르면서 겁 없이 달려드는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for charging into something fearlessly without understanding it.

explain_en: It is used when someone does something without knowing how things work or what is really going on. It almost always appears as '멋모르고' or '멋모르는 + noun'. It is a '르'-irregular verb like '모르다', so the 해요 form is '멋몰라요'. Compared with a plain '모르고', it feels like acting innocently or carelessly because you don't know the situation.

t90.ax: I was a clueless newcomer, so I made many mistakes.

examples.ko: 강아지가 배를 보이며 발라당 누웠어요.
examples.en: The puppy flopped onto its back and showed its belly.

examples.ko: 고양이가 햇볕 아래에서 발라당 드러누웠어요.
examples.en: The cat rolled onto its back in the sunshine.

examples.ko: 아이가 미끄러져서 발라당 뒤로 넘어졌어요.
examples.en: The child slipped and fell flat on his back.

examples.ko: 피곤해서 침대에 발라당 누워 버렸어요.
examples.en: I was tired, so I just flopped down onto the bed.

examples.ko: 바닥에 발라당 눕자 몸이 편해졌어요.
examples.en: When I lay flat on the floor, my body relaxed.

examples.ko: 거북이가 뒤집혀 발라당 누운 채 버둥거렸어요.
examples.en: The turtle was flipped over on its back, struggling.

explain: 가볍게 뒤로 눕거나 넘어지는 모습이고, 강아지, 고양이, 아기처럼 귀여운 대상에 잘 어울려요. 더 크고 둔한 느낌은 '벌러덩'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The baby fell flat on its back while walking.
phrases.nuance_ko: '눕다' 대신 갑자기 뒤로 넘어지는 모습을 가볍고 귀엽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Instead of simply lying down, this describes falling backward suddenly, in a light and cute way.
phrases.en_equiv: to fall flat on one's back

phrases.example: 강아지가 소파 위에 발라당 누워 있어요.
phrases.en: The puppy is lying on its back on the sofa.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누운 채로 있는 상태를 말해요. 배를 보이고 편하게 쉬는 동물에게 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: This describes staying in a lying position, and suits animals relaxing with their bellies up.
phrases.en_equiv: to be lying on one's back

phrases.en: The man was tired and flopped down on the floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '발라당'보다 크고 둔한 느낌이라 어른이나 큰 대상에게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It feels bigger and clumsier than 발라당, so it is used for adults or large things.

explain_en: It describes lightly flopping or falling onto one's back, and suits cute subjects like puppies, cats and babies. The bigger, heavier version is '벌러덩'.

t90.ax: The child slipped and fell flat on his back.

examples.ko: 운동을 습관화하면 몸이 훨씬 가벼워져요.
examples.en: If you make exercise a habit, your body feels much lighter.

examples.ko: 책 읽기를 습관화하려고 매일 밤 20분씩 읽어요.
examples.en: To make reading a habit, I read for 20 minutes every night.

examples.ko: 일찍 자는 것을 습관화해서 이제 아침이 힘들지 않아요.
examples.en: I made going to bed early a habit, so mornings aren't hard anymore.

examples.ko: 처음부터 너무 많이 하지 말고 조금씩 습관화하세요.
examples.en: Don't do too much at first; build it into a habit little by little.

examples.ko: 저축을 습관화한 뒤로 돈이 조금씩 모였어요.
examples.en: Since I made saving a habit, my money has slowly piled up.

examples.ko: 좋은 행동을 습관화하는 데에는 시간이 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes time to turn good behavior into a habit.

explain: '~을/를 습관화하다'로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '습관을 들이다'가 더 흔하고, 습관화하다는 글이나 강의, 건강 정보에서 자주 보여요. 목표가 되는 행동 앞에 '운동, 독서, 저축'을 붙여요.

phrases.en: Getting up early has become a habit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 하는 것이 아니라 어떤 행동이 자연스러운 습관이 된 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a behavior that has become a natural habit, rather than something you actively do.

phrases.en: I got into the habit of drinking water every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '습관화하다' 대신 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The more common everyday alternative to 습관화하다.

phrases.example: 하루에 삼십 분 걷기를 습관화해 보세요.
phrases.en: Try making a thirty-minute daily walk a habit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건강 정보나 조언에서 권할 때 '-아/어 보세요'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Typical in health tips and advice, with -아/어 보세요 to suggest trying.

explain_en: It takes an object: '~을/를 습관화하다'. In everyday talk '습관을 들이다' is more natural, while 습관화하다 shows up in writing, lectures and health advice. Put the target behavior before it, such as exercise, reading or saving.

t90.ax: It takes time to turn good behavior into a habit.

examples.ko: 일요일 오후에 동네를 어슬렁어슬렁 걸어 다녔어요.
examples.en: On Sunday afternoon I strolled around the neighborhood.

examples.ko: 고양이가 마당을 어슬렁어슬렁 돌아다니고 있어요.
examples.en: The cat is prowling around the yard.

examples.ko: 수업이 끝났는데도 그는 어슬렁어슬렁 교실을 나갔어요.
examples.en: Even though class was over, he sauntered out of the classroom.

examples.ko: 급할 것 없다는 듯이 어슬렁어슬렁 걸어오네요.
examples.en: He's ambling over as if he's in no hurry at all.

examples.ko: 약속 시각이 한 시간이나 넘어서야 그는 어슬렁어슬렁 나타났어요.
examples.en: He only sauntered in after the meeting time was over by a whole hour.

examples.ko: 시장 안을 어슬렁어슬렁 구경하다 보면 시간이 금방 가요.
examples.en: If you wander around the market looking at things, time flies.

explain: '느릿느릿'이 속도만 말한다면 '어슬렁어슬렁'은 뚜렷한 목적 없이 여유롭게, 때로는 게으르게 걷는 모습까지 보여 줘요. '어슬렁거리다'처럼 동사로도 자주 말해요. 급한 일이 있는 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: A man is loitering in front of the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사 '어슬렁어슬렁'을 동사로 바꾼 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form built from the adverb 어슬렁어슬렁.

phrases.en: The kids are wandering around the playground.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어슬렁거리다'와 거의 같고 조금 더 말투가 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 어슬렁거리다 but a bit more casual.

phrases.example: 그는 주머니에 손을 넣고 어슬렁어슬렁 걸어갔어요.
phrases.en: He strolled off with his hands in his pockets.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서두르지 않고 여유롭게 걸어가는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows someone walking off in a relaxed, unhurried way.

explain_en: While '느릿느릿' only describes slow speed, '어슬렁어슬렁' also shows walking around without a clear purpose, in a relaxed or sometimes lazy way. People also use the verb form '어슬렁거리다'. You would not use it for someone who has something urgent to do.

examples.ko: 지금 요러다 정말 늦겠어요, 빨리 나가요.
examples.en: If we keep doing this we'll really be late, so let's go quickly.

examples.ko: 창문을 열고 계속 요러다가 감기 걸리겠어요.
examples.en: If you keep doing this with the window open, you'll catch a cold.

examples.ko: 아까부터 왜 자꾸 저한테 요러세요?
examples.en: Why do you keep doing this to me since a while ago?

examples.ko: 아이가 밥 먹을 때 요러면 어떻게 해야 해요?
examples.en: What should I do if my child acts like this at mealtime?

examples.ko: 요러지 말고 이쪽으로 와서 같이 앉아요.
examples.en: Don't be like that, come over here and sit with us.

examples.ko: 둘이 요러고 있으니 웃음이 나요.
examples.en: Seeing the two of you carry on like this makes me laugh.

explain: '이러다'를 작고 귀엽게 말하는 구어로, 장난스럽거나 살짝 못마땅할 때 써요. 윗사람에게 쓰면 버릇없게 들릴 수 있어요. '요러다가', '요러면', '요러지 말고'처럼 활용해서 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: If you keep doing this, you'll fall. Go slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 하는 행동이 계속되면 안 좋은 일이 생길 것 같을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when continuing the current action might lead to something bad.

phrases.en: You shouldn't do this to a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 하는 행동을 가볍게 말리거나 타이를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to gently stop or scold someone for what they are doing now.

phrases.en: Don't be like this, come and sit over here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하던 행동을 멈추고 다른 것을 하자고 권할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to suggest stopping what someone is doing and doing something else.

explain_en: It is a small, cute variant of '이러다', used playfully or when mildly displeased. It can sound rude toward a superior. It is most often heard as '요러다가', '요러면' or '요러지 말고'.

examples.ko: 우리 강아지가 바닥을 킁킁거리며 돌아다녀요.
examples.en: My puppy goes around sniffing the floor.

examples.ko: 동생이 무슨 냄새인지 한참 킁킁거려요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has been sniffing for a while to figure out the smell.

examples.ko: 고양이가 낯선 가방을 한참 킁킁거렸어요.
examples.en: The cat sniffed the unfamiliar bag for a long time.

examples.ko: 코가 막혀서 자꾸 킁킁거리게 돼요.
examples.en: My nose is stuffed, so I keep sniffling.

examples.ko: 그만 킁킁거리고 와서 밥 먹어요.
examples.en: Stop sniffing around and come eat.

examples.ko: 경찰견이 가방 냄새를 킁킁거리다가 멈췄어요.
examples.en: The police dog sniffed the bag and then stopped.

explain: 코로 냄새를 맡으려고 숨을 짧게 자꾸 들이쉬는 소리나 모습이에요. 강아지나 고양이에게 많이 쓰고, 코가 막혔을 때도 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 조금 우스꽝스럽거나 장난스러운 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: The cat is sniffing around the new bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: '킁킁거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 조금 더 입말 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as '킁킁거리다', with a slightly more spoken feel.

phrases.en: The puppy sniffs the treat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'로 이어서 냄새를 맡는 동작을 자세히 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Connected with '-며' to describe the sniffing action in detail.

phrases.en: The sniffing puppy is so cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form before a noun.

explain_en: It describes taking short, repeated sniffs through the nose to smell something, or the sound of that. It is often used for dogs and cats, and also for a stuffy nose. Used for a person, it sounds a little comical or playful.

examples.ko: 이 정책은 사회의 퇴보라고 비판받아요.
examples.en: This policy is criticized as a step backward for society.

examples.ko: 연습을 안 하면 실력이 퇴보로 이어져요.
examples.en: If you don't practice, your skills end up going backward.

examples.ko: 변화가 없으면 그것은 곧 퇴보예요.
examples.en: If there's no change, that is in itself a step backward.

examples.ko: 저는 이 결정이 문화의 퇴보를 부른다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think this decision will bring about a decline in culture.

examples.ko: 한 걸음 물러서는 것이 꼭 퇴보는 아니에요.
examples.en: Stepping back isn't necessarily regression.

examples.ko: 교육 환경이 퇴보 없이 계속 좋아지면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope the educational environment keeps improving without going backward.

explain: '발전'과 짝을 이루는 반대말로 자주 나와요. 명사로는 '퇴보를 부르다', '퇴보로 이어지다'처럼 쓰고, 동사로는 '퇴보하다'를 더 많이 써요. 일상에서는 '실력이 떨어졌어요'라고 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 연습을 안 하는 습관이 퇴보로 이어져요.
phrases.en: The habit of not practicing leads to decline.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 행동이나 태도가 나빠지는 결과를 만든다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an action or attitude results in decline.

phrases.en: If you don't make an effort, your skills decline.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '퇴보'의 동사형으로, 실제 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 퇴보, used more often in actual speech.

phrases.en: After a break, my skills dropped.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '퇴보' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday way to say what 퇴보 means.

explain_en: It often appears as the opposite of '발전' (progress). As a noun it is used as '퇴보를 부르다' or '퇴보로 이어지다', while the verb '퇴보하다' is more common. In daily talk people may say '실력이 떨어졌어요'.

examples.ko: 추운 날에는 언 손을 호호 불면 조금 따뜻해져요.
examples.en: On cold days, blowing warm breath on your frozen hands warms them up a little.

examples.ko: 아이가 뜨거운 죽을 호호 불어서 먹어요.
examples.en: The child blows on the hot porridge to cool it before eating.

examples.ko: 엄마가 다친 손가락에 호호 불어 줬어요.
examples.en: Mom blew softly on my hurt finger.

examples.ko: 안경에 입김을 호호 불고 천으로 닦았어요.
examples.en: I breathed on my glasses and wiped them with a cloth.

examples.ko: 갓 구운 호떡을 호호 불며 길에서 먹었어요.
examples.en: I ate a freshly made hotteok on the street, blowing on it.

examples.ko: 장갑을 안 껴서 손을 호호 불며 걸었어요.
examples.en: I had no gloves, so I walked blowing on my hands.

explain: 입을 동그랗게 하고 따뜻한 입김을 내보내는 소리나 모양이에요. 보통 '호호 불다'로 써요. 웃음소리 '호호'와 소리는 같지만 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: Mom blew softly on my wound for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아픈 곳을 달래 주려고 입김을 불어 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when blowing warm breath on a sore spot to comfort someone.

phrases.en: I blew on the hot tea to cool it down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜨거운 음식이나 음료를 식힐 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to cool hot food or drinks.

phrases.en: I ate the fish-shaped pastry while blowing on it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜨거운 음식을 조심해서 먹는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes eating hot food carefully.
phrases.en_equiv: to eat while blowing on it

explain_en: It describes the sound or look of rounding your mouth and letting out warm breath. It is usually used as '호호 불다'. It sounds the same as the laughing sound '호호', but it is a different word.

t90.ax: Mom blew softly on my hurt finger.

examples.ko: 그는 질문을 회피하고 대답하지 않았어요.
examples.en: He dodged the question and didn't answer.

examples.ko: 책임을 회피하면 신뢰를 잃어요.
examples.en: If you evade responsibility, you lose trust.

examples.ko: 사고를 회피하려고 급하게 브레이크를 밟았어요.
examples.en: I hit the brakes hard to avoid an accident.

examples.ko: 눈을 마주치는 것을 회피하는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Some people avoid making eye contact.

examples.ko: 어려운 문제를 계속 회피할 수는 없어요.
examples.en: You can't keep dodging a difficult problem.

examples.ko: 그는 갈등을 회피하다가 더 큰 문제를 만들었어요.
examples.en: He dodged the conflict and ended up creating a bigger problem.

explain: 회피하다는 책임, 질문, 갈등, 사람처럼 마주하기 싫은 것을 일부러 피할 때 써요. '피하다'는 비를 피하다처럼 넓게 쓰고, 회피하다는 일부러 마주하지 않는다는 비판적인 느낌이 있어요. 책임, 질문, 시선과 잘 어울려요.

phrases.example: 그는 내 눈을 피하고 아무 말도 안 했어요.
phrases.en: He avoided my eyes and said nothing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '회피하다'보다 넓게 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요. 비나 사람, 위험도 피할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader, easier word than 회피하다; you can avoid rain, people or danger.

phrases.en: If you made a mistake, don't dodge responsibility; apologize.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책임, 질문, 문제와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with responsibility, questions and problems.

phrases.en: She dodged the answer and changed the subject.
phrases.nuance_ko: 질문을 받고 일부러 답하지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone is asked a question and deliberately doesn't answer.

explain_en: 회피하다 is used when you deliberately stay away from something you don't want to face, such as responsibility, a question, a conflict or a person. 피하다 is broad, as in avoiding rain, while 회피하다 carries a critical feel of deliberately not facing it. It pairs well with responsibility, questions and eye contact.

t90.ax: Some people avoid making eye contact.

examples.ko: 처음 만난 선배에게 반말을 하다니 정말 건방지네요.
examples.en: Using casual speech to a senior you just met is really cheeky.

examples.ko: 말투가 건방지다는 말을 들어서 요즘은 말끝을 조심해요.
examples.en: I was told my tone is cheeky, so I watch how I end my sentences these days.

examples.ko: 건방 떨지 말고 선배님께 먼저 인사해요.
examples.en: Don't be cocky, and greet your senior first.

examples.ko: 그 후배가 건방을 떨어서 다들 불편해해요.
examples.en: That junior acts cocky, so everyone feels uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 아이가 건방진 표정으로 팔짱을 꼈어요.
examples.en: The child crossed his arms with a cheeky look.

examples.ko: 어른한테 그렇게 말하면 건방져 보여요.
examples.en: If you talk to an adult like that, you come across as rude.

explain: 보통 '건방지다'로 쓰고, 명사 '건방'은 '건방을 떨다/부리다'처럼 말해요. 어린 사람이나 아랫사람이 버릇없이 잘난 척할 때 쓰는 말이라, 윗사람을 이렇게 말하지는 않아요.

phrases.en: That junior has a somewhat cocky way of speaking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '건방'보다 일상에서 훨씬 자주 쓰는 형용사 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form, used far more often than the noun '건방'.

phrases.en: Don't get cocky just because you're a little good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘난 척하며 버릇없이 굴 때 쓰는 짝말이에요. '건방을 부리다'도 비슷해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for acting arrogant and rude; '건방을 부리다' is similar.

phrases.en: A cocky way of speaking is rude to elders.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 형태로, 말투나 태도를 나쁘게 평가할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form used to criticize someone's tone or attitude.

explain_en: It is usually used as '건방지다', and the noun appears as '건방을 떨다/부리다'. It describes a younger or lower-ranked person acting rude and full of themselves, so it is not used to describe a superior.

t90.ax: Don't be cocky, and greet your senior first.

examples.ko: 이번 시험에는 고난도 문제가 많았어요.
examples.en: There were many high-difficulty questions on this exam.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 고난도 기술을 성공시켰어요.
examples.en: That athlete pulled off a highly difficult move.

examples.ko: 고난도 요리라서 초보자에게는 어려워요.
examples.en: It's an advanced dish, so it's hard for beginners.

examples.ko: 이 수학 문제집은 고난도 문제만 모아 놓았어요.
examples.en: This math workbook collects only hard problems.

examples.ko: 고난도 수술을 무사히 마쳤다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the highly difficult surgery ended safely.

examples.ko: 처음부터 고난도 수업을 듣지 말고 쉬운 것부터 하세요.
examples.en: Don't take an advanced class from the start; begin with an easy one.

explain: '난이도가 높은'을 짧게 말한 느낌으로, 문제·기술·수술·요리 앞에 붙여 써요. 반대로 쉬울 때는 '난도가 낮은'이나 그냥 '쉬운'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The last question was a high-difficulty one, so it was hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험이나 숙제에서 매우 어려운 문제를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a very hard question on a test or homework.

phrases.example: 체조 선수가 고난도 기술을 보여 줬어요.
phrases.en: The gymnast showed a highly difficult move.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동이나 공연에서 하기 어려운 동작에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for hard moves in sports or performances.

phrases.en: This dish has a high level of difficulty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고난도'를 풀어서 말한 표현으로 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spelled-out version of 고난도 that sounds more natural in speech.

explain_en: It is a short way of saying 'high in difficulty' and goes before words like problem, technique, surgery or dish. For the opposite, say '난도가 낮은' or simply '쉬운'.

t90.ax: This math workbook collects only hard problems.

en: to be headstrong; to be willful

examples.ko: 할아버지는 조금 고집스러운 분이에요.
examples.en: My grandfather is a bit of a stubborn person.

examples.ko: 동생은 어릴 때부터 고집스러웠어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has been stubborn since childhood.

examples.ko: 그렇게 고집스럽게 말하면 아무도 안 들어요.
examples.en: If you speak so stubbornly, nobody will listen.

examples.ko: 고집스러워 보이지만 사실은 마음이 따뜻해요.
examples.en: He looks stubborn, but actually he is warm-hearted.

examples.ko: 고집스럽고 말이 없어서 친해지기 어려웠어요.
examples.en: He was stubborn and quiet, so it was hard to get close to him.

examples.ko: 고집스러울 때는 한 발 물러서는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: When you're being stubborn, it's good to step back.

explain: '고집이 세다'와 비슷하지만 '고집스럽다'는 보기에 고집이 센 모습이라는 말투예요. '고집이 세다'는 성격을 말하고, '고집스럽다'는 표정, 말투, 행동에서 느껴지는 모습을 말해요. 대부분은 약간 부정적으로 들려요.

phrases.en: The child stood there with a stubborn look.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼굴에서 느껴지는 고집을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for stubbornness that you can see on someone's face.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 고집스럽게 자기 의견만 말했어요.
phrases.en: He stubbornly kept stating only his own opinion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행동하는 방식이 고집스러울 때 부사로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form, for when someone acts in a stubborn way.

phrases.en: That teacher looks a little stubborn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습으로 받은 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an impression based on how someone looks.

explain_en: Similar to 고집이 세다 (be strong-willed), but 고집스럽다 describes a stubbornness you can see in someone's face, tone or behavior. 고집이 세다 talks about character itself. It is usually mildly negative.
